57acb942970b: Ask: «Co dziś jadłeś / jadłaś na śniadanie?». Let them answer as well as they can, note 1–2 mistakes — you will come back to them at s5.
5ad2386cb9cd: After each row the student orders a dish of their own in that gender: «Poproszę…». The feminine is the main source of mistakes.
5780ab5d16e3: Quick round: you name two items from the menu («żurek + kawa», «sałatka + woda»), the student builds a full sentence using the formula.
36570c5f35f4: Ask the student to write a “shopping list” of 4 items: «kilo…, butelka…, trochę…». Plural genitive (jabłek, pomidorów) is for recognition only, not for cramming.
dd4871b9156e: Play host: you ask «Smakuje ci…? / Smakują ci…?» about different dishes, the student answers in full sentences. Watch smakuje/smakują.
b761a59f08cb: Ask: «Co jesz na śniadanie? Co pijesz do obiadu? Kawa z czym?». The student answers using the right preposition.
4832f58f3121: Don't give a rule «always -a»: the norm allows variants. It's enough that the student recognizes «pączka, banana, ogórka, schabowego» and doesn't treat them as a mistake.
d7d748ebb4cf: Say each trap in English first and let the student translate it themselves — only then reveal the correct version.
79f4609968d9: Owoce means fruit: jabłka, gruszki. Warzywa means vegetables: marchewka, kapusta.
386b90abff90: Dynia to pumpkin. Słodki żółty owoc to melon.
d935ff512d1f: “Owoce/warzywa” get mixed up even at B1 — catch it by ear until the end of the lesson. “Dynia” will come back in dialogue c1.
